summary: caspian-client performs install- and import-time host reconnaissance uploaded to a third-party Sentry endpoint
details: caspian_client 2.9.10 invokes report_environment() from setup.py, the PEP 517 build backend (backend.py), and caspian_client/__init__.py, so the function runs on sdist build, on pip install, and on every import of the package. The function's try-body references a misspelled attribute (env.wheel_platfrom, while the real attribute is wheel_platform), guaranteeing an AttributeError on every call; the except branch then invokes capture_exception() against a hardcoded Sentry DSN at o4512443838169088.ingest.us.sentry.io. The uploaded payload is assembled by _common_fields and _process_tree and contains socket.gethostname(), the inferred public IP address, and an enumeration of other processes on the host obtained by iterating /proc and reading /proc/<pid>/cmdline, /proc/<pid>/comm, and /proc/<pid>/stat for processes beyond the package's own. The package advertises itself as a data-platform API client, and its declared Homepage/Documentation URLs point at caspian.internal, a reserved non-resolvable TLD, so the publisher cannot be verified as a legitimate internal publisher on public PyPI. The always-throwing attribute access, the breadth of host and process data collected, the use of a third-party ingestion endpoint rather than the package's own documented API, and the lack of any relation between host/process reconnaissance and the stated client functionality together form an exfiltration pattern rather than legitimate error telemetry.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
